checks.title: PREADY only in an Access cycle
checks.behavior: At every rising edge of i_clk_core with i_rst_n_core=1: if o_apb_pready=1, then i_apb_psel=1 and i_apb_penable=1 at the same edge.

checks.title: PREADY is a single-cycle pulse
checks.behavior: If o_apb_pready=1 at a rising edge N and i_rst_n_core=1 at edges N and N+1, then o_apb_pready=0 at rising edge N+1.

checks.title: PSLVERR only with PREADY
checks.behavior: At every rising edge of i_clk_core (reset asserted or not): if o_apb_pslverr=1, then o_apb_pready=1 at the same edge.

checks.title: PRDATA holds its value outside PREADY cycles
checks.behavior: At a rising edge N with i_rst_n_core=1 at edges N-1 and N: if o_apb_prdata at edge N differs from o_apb_prdata at edge N-1, then o_apb_pready=1 at edge N. In other words, o_apb_prdata changes only in a cycle where PREADY is high.

checks.title: Both sides idle in the Setup cycle
checks.behavior: At every rising edge with i_rst_n_core=1, i_apb_psel=1 and i_apb_penable=0 (a Setup cycle, including one right after a PREADY cycle with i_apb_psel held at 1): o_apb_pready=0 and o_tlul_a_valid=0 at that same edge.

checks.title: Channel A constant fields and legal encoding
checks.behavior: At every rising edge of i_clk_core, whether reset is asserted or not: o_tlul_a_param=3'b000, o_tlul_a_size=2'b10, o_tlul_a_mask=4'b1111, o_tlul_a_source=PARA_SRC_ID, o_tlul_a_user=all zeros (PARA_A_USER_W bits), o_tlul_a_opcode[1:0]=2'b00, o_tlul_a_address[1:0]=2'b00, and o_tlul_a_opcode is either 3'b000 or 3'b100. 3'b001 (PutPartialData) and undefined opcodes never appear.

checks.title: Channel A held stable until accepted
checks.behavior: If o_tlul_a_valid=1 and i_tlul_a_ready=0 at a rising edge N, and i_rst_n_core=1 at edges N and N+1, then at rising edge N+1 o_tlul_a_valid=1 and o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address, o_tlul_a_data, o_tlul_a_param, o_tlul_a_size, o_tlul_a_mask, o_tlul_a_source and o_tlul_a_user are unchanged from edge N.

checks.title: A_VALID drops right after acceptance (one request per handshake)
checks.behavior: If o_tlul_a_valid=1 and i_tlul_a_ready=1 at a rising edge N, and i_rst_n_core=1 at edges N and N+1, then o_tlul_a_valid=0 at rising edge N+1.

checks.title: A TL-UL request starts only after a legal Setup
checks.behavior: If o_tlul_a_valid=0 at rising edge N-1 and o_tlul_a_valid=1 at rising edge N, with i_rst_n_core=1 at both edges, then at edge N-1: i_apb_psel=1, i_apb_penable=0, i_apb_paddr[1:0]=2'b00, and (i_apb_pwrite=0 or i_apb_pstrb=4'b1111).

checks.title: Early launch of a legal request in the first Access cycle
checks.behavior: Call a rising edge N a legal Setup edge when i_rst_n_core=1, i_apb_psel=1, i_apb_penable=0, i_apb_paddr[1:0]=2'b00 and (i_apb_pwrite=0 or i_apb_pstrb=4'b1111). If i_rst_n_core=1 at edge N+1, then at edge N+1: o_tlul_a_valid=1; o_tlul_a_opcode=3'b000 if i_apb_pwrite was 1 at edge N, or 3'b100 if it was 0; o_tlul_a_address equals i_apb_paddr sampled at edge N; o_tlul_a_data equals i_apb_pwdata sampled at edge N when i_apb_pwrite was 1; o_tlul_d_ready=1; o_apb_pready=0. This holds for every such Setup edge, including one in the cycle right after a PREADY cycle with i_apb_psel held at 1.

checks.title: Local error completion for an illegal request
checks.behavior: Call a rising edge N an illegal Setup edge when i_rst_n_core=1, i_apb_psel=1, i_apb_penable=0, and either i_apb_paddr[1:0]!=2'b00 or (i_apb_pwrite=1 and i_apb_pstrb!=4'b1111). If i_rst_n_core=1 at edge N+1, then at edge N+1 (the first Access cycle): o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=1, o_apb_prdata=32'h0 and o_tlul_a_valid=0.

checks.title: Accepted TL-UL response is mapped to the APB completion in the next cycle
checks.behavior: The checker keeps two state variables, built only from port values sampled at rising edges and cleared while i_rst_n_core=0: pend (a request has been accepted and its response not yet counted) and pend_rd (o_tlul_a_opcode[2] of that request). At edge N, a response counts (resp_cnt) when i_tlul_d_valid=1, o_tlul_d_ready=1, and either (o_tlul_a_valid=1 and i_tlul_a_ready=1) or pend=1. Here rd=pend_rd if pend=1, otherwise rd=o_tlul_a_opcode[2]. pend is updated at each edge to ((o_tlul_a_valid & i_tlul_a_ready) | pend) & ~resp_cnt, and pend_rd loads o_tlul_a_opcode[2] on acceptance. Property: if resp_cnt at edge N and i_rst_n_core=1 at edge N+1, then at edge N+1 o_apb_pready=1 and o_apb_pslverr=err, where err = i_tlul_d_error | (i_tlul_d_opcode != (rd ? 3'b001 : 3'b000)) | (i_tlul_d_source != PARA_SRC_ID), all sampled at edge N. Also at edge N+1, o_apb_prdata = i_tlul_d_data sampled at edge N when rd=1 and err=0; otherwise o_apb_prdata = 32'h0.

checks.title: PREADY only as the result of a request; orphan responses have no APB effect
checks.behavior: If o_apb_pready=1 at rising edge N, with i_rst_n_core=1 at edges N-1 and N, then at edge N-1 either an illegal Setup edge (as defined in CHK-011) occurred or a response counted (resp_cnt as defined in CHK-012). An i_tlul_d_valid=1 that does not count (orphan) therefore never leads to o_apb_pready=1. Together with CHK-003 and CHK-004, it also never changes o_apb_pslverr or o_apb_prdata.

checks.title: At most one TL-UL request outstanding, none before the APB completion
checks.behavior: Call edge N an a_valid rise edge when o_tlul_a_valid=0 at edge N-1 and o_tlul_a_valid=1 at edge N. Between any two consecutive a_valid rise edges N1 < N2 with no reset between them, there is exactly one rising edge M in [N1, N2) at which o_tlul_a_valid=1 and i_tlul_a_ready=1, and at least one rising edge in (N1, N2) at which o_apb_pready=1.

checks.title: D_READY is 0 in reset and 1 from the first edge after release
checks.behavior: At every rising edge at which i_rst_n_core=0, o_tlul_d_ready=0. At every rising edge N at which i_rst_n_core=1 and i_rst_n_core was also 1 at edge N-1, o_tlul_d_ready=1.

checks.title: Output values in reset and at the first edge after release
checks.behavior: At every rising edge N at which i_rst_n_core=0, and also at the first rising edge with i_rst_n_core=1 after an edge with i_rst_n_core=0, these outputs are 0: o_tlul_a_valid, o_tlul_d_ready, o_apb_pready, o_apb_pslverr, o_apb_prdata (32'h0), o_tlul_a_opcode (3'b000), o_tlul_a_address (0), o_tlul_a_data (32'h0).

checks.title: Asynchronous reset assertion and synchronous release
checks.behavior: Reset asserts asynchronously: outputs are cleared without waiting for a clock edge. After a synchronous release, every output starts from its defined reset value.
checks.stimulus: Run a legal write with a nonzero address and data whose response is held back by the device (i_tlul_a_ready=0), so o_tlul_a_valid=1 and o_tlul_a_address, o_tlul_a_data and o_tlul_a_opcode are nonzero. Drive i_rst_n_core to 0 between two rising edges of i_clk_core. Hold it low for 3 cycles with i_apb_psel=0, then release it synchronously to a rising edge. Repeat the async assertion after a completed read with nonzero o_apb_prdata, and after a local error with o_apb_pslverr=1 in its PREADY cycle.
checks.expected: Within the same clock cycle that i_rst_n_core falls, before the next rising edge, these outputs are all 0: o_tlul_a_valid, o_tlul_d_ready, o_apb_pready, o_apb_pslverr, o_apb_prdata, o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address, o_tlul_a_data. They stay 0 while reset is low. o_tlul_a_param=3'b000, o_tlul_a_size=2'b10, o_tlul_a_mask=4'b1111, o_tlul_a_source=PARA_SRC_ID and o_tlul_a_user=0 throughout. o_tlul_d_ready is still 0 when sampled at the first rising edge after release and is 1 at every later edge. A legal transfer after release completes normally (CHK-019 timing).

checks.title: Reset during a transfer abandons it
checks.behavior: A transfer in progress when reset asserts is abandoned. No APB completion is produced for it after release.
checks.stimulus: For each of A1 (o_tlul_a_valid=1, i_tlul_a_ready=0), A2 (request accepted, i_tlul_d_valid not yet given) and A3 (the o_apb_pready=1 cycle), assert i_rst_n_core in that cycle of a legal read, and in a separate run of a legal write. The APB requester and TL-UL device models are reset with the bridge and stop driving that transfer (i_apb_psel=0, i_tlul_d_valid=0). Release reset, wait 5 idle cycles, then run one legal read and one legal write with a prompt device.
checks.expected: After release, o_apb_pready, o_apb_pslverr and o_tlul_a_valid stay 0 during the 5 idle cycles, so there is no completion for the abandoned transfer. The two following transfers each produce exactly one TL-UL request and one completion with the correct data. Each takes 3 Access cycles, and the first Setup after release is followed by o_tlul_a_valid=1 at the next edge.

checks.title: Directed aligned full-strobe write to a prompt device
checks.behavior: An aligned write with PSTRB=4'b1111 becomes one PutFullData. It completes after 3 Access cycles with PSLVERR=0 and PRDATA=0.
checks.stimulus: After reset, drive APB writes with i_apb_paddr[1:0]=2'b00 (random upper bits), i_apb_pstrb=4'b1111 and random i_apb_pwdata. Use one Setup cycle, then hold i_apb_penable=1 until o_apb_pready. The device drives i_tlul_a_ready=1 in the first cycle o_tlul_a_valid=1 (A1), then i_tlul_d_valid=1 for one cycle in the next cycle (A2) with i_tlul_d_opcode=3'b000, i_tlul_d_error=0, i_tlul_d_source=PARA_SRC_ID and random i_tlul_d_data.
checks.expected: In A1 (the cycle after Setup): o_tlul_a_valid=1, o_tlul_a_opcode=3'b000, o_tlul_a_size=2'b10, o_tlul_a_mask=4'b1111, o_tlul_a_address=PADDR, o_tlul_a_data=PWDATA, o_tlul_a_source=PARA_SRC_ID. o_tlul_a_valid=0 in A2. In A3: o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=0, o_apb_prdata=32'h0. The Access phase lasts exactly 3 cycles (2 wait states), and there is exactly one TL-UL handshake per transfer.

checks.title: Directed and random aligned reads, PSTRB ignored
checks.behavior: An aligned read becomes one Get whatever the PSTRB value, and PRDATA returns d_data after 3 Access cycles.
checks.stimulus: Drive aligned APB reads (i_apb_pwrite=0, i_apb_paddr[1:0]=2'b00) with i_apb_pstrb=4'b0000, and also with random nonzero values including 4'b1111 and partial ones. Use a prompt device: i_tlul_a_ready=1 in A1, and one-cycle i_tlul_d_valid in A2 with i_tlul_d_opcode=3'b001, i_tlul_d_error=0, i_tlul_d_source=PARA_SRC_ID and random i_tlul_d_data.
checks.expected: For every PSTRB value: o_tlul_a_valid=1 in A1 with o_tlul_a_opcode=3'b100, o_tlul_a_size=2'b10, o_tlul_a_mask=4'b1111, o_tlul_a_address=PADDR. In A3: o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=0, o_apb_prdata = the i_tlul_d_data driven in A2. The Access phase lasts exactly 3 cycles. Results do not depend on i_apb_pstrb.

checks.title: Response in the acceptance cycle
checks.behavior: A response given in the same cycle as the request acceptance is used. PREADY is then 1 in the second Access cycle.
checks.stimulus: For a legal read and a legal write, the device drives i_tlul_a_ready=1 and i_tlul_d_valid=1 together in A1 (the first cycle o_tlul_a_valid=1), with the correct d_opcode (3'b001 for read, 3'b000 for write), i_tlul_d_error=0, i_tlul_d_source=PARA_SRC_ID and random i_tlul_d_data. No later d_valid.
checks.expected: In A2: o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=0, o_apb_prdata = d_data for the read and 32'h0 for the write. o_tlul_a_valid=0 in A2. The Access phase lasts exactly 2 cycles (1 wait state).

checks.title: Unsupported write strobe gives a local error
checks.behavior: A write with any PSTRB other than 4'b1111 completes in the first Access cycle with PSLVERR and issues no TL-UL request. The next Setup is accepted in the cycle after PREADY.
checks.stimulus: Drive aligned writes (i_apb_paddr[1:0]=2'b00) with each of the 15 i_apb_pstrb values other than 4'b1111, including 4'b0000, with random i_apb_pwdata. After each, put a legal write or read Setup in the cycle right after the PREADY cycle (i_apb_psel held at 1). The device is prompt and also sends no response unless a request was presented.
checks.expected: For each illegal-strobe write: o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=1 and o_apb_prdata=32'h0 in the first Access cycle (Access phase = 1 cycle, 0 wait states). o_tlul_a_valid stays 0 from the Setup until the next Setup. The following legal transfer gets o_tlul_a_valid=1 in the cycle after its Setup, and its Setup-to-Setup interval with the error transfer is 2 cycles.

checks.title: Misaligned address gives a local error
checks.behavior: A read or write with PADDR[1:0] other than 2'b00 completes in the first Access cycle with PSLVERR and issues no TL-UL request.
checks.stimulus: Drive reads (any i_apb_pstrb) and writes with i_apb_pstrb=4'b1111 and with partial strobes, using i_apb_paddr[1:0] in {2'b01, 2'b10, 2'b11} and random upper bits. Follow each with a legal transfer in the next cycle after PREADY.
checks.expected: For each misaligned access: o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=1 and o_apb_prdata=32'h0 in the first Access cycle (1 Access cycle). o_tlul_a_valid=0 throughout. The next legal transfer starts with o_tlul_a_valid=1 in the cycle after its Setup.

checks.title: TL-UL d_error is mapped to PSLVERR
checks.behavior: A response with d_error=1 completes the APB transfer with PSLVERR=1 and PRDATA=0.
checks.stimulus: Legal reads and writes with a prompt device and with a same-cycle response. The response has i_tlul_d_error=1, the correct d_opcode, i_tlul_d_source=PARA_SRC_ID and nonzero random i_tlul_d_data.
checks.expected: In the PREADY cycle (A3 for prompt, A2 for same-cycle): o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=1, o_apb_prdata=32'h0, for both the read and the write. Exactly one TL-UL request per transfer.

checks.title: Wrong d_opcode or wrong d_source is mapped to PSLVERR
checks.behavior: A response whose opcode does not match the request type, or whose source differs from PARA_SRC_ID, completes with PSLVERR=1 and PRDATA=0.
checks.stimulus: Legal reads answered with i_tlul_d_opcode in {3'b000, 3'b010, 3'b011, 3'b100..3'b111}. Legal writes answered with i_tlul_d_opcode in {3'b001, 3'b010, ..., 3'b111}. Then legal reads and writes answered with the correct opcode but i_tlul_d_source != PARA_SRC_ID: each single bit flipped, plus random values. All with i_tlul_d_error=0, nonzero i_tlul_d_data, and the prompt-device timing.
checks.expected: Each such transfer completes in A3 with o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=1 and o_apb_prdata=32'h0. Control cases with i_tlul_d_opcode=3'b001 for reads, 3'b000 for writes and i_tlul_d_source=PARA_SRC_ID complete with o_apb_pslverr=0, and the read returns d_data.

checks.title: Channel A back pressure
checks.behavior: While i_tlul_a_ready is low, channel A stays valid and stable and the APB Access phase is extended. The request is accepted exactly once.
checks.stimulus: Legal reads and writes where the device holds i_tlul_a_ready=0 for D cycles after o_tlul_a_valid rises, with D in 0..8, then drives i_tlul_a_ready=1 for one cycle. It answers in the next cycle (also a same-cycle variant). Random address, data and D.
checks.expected: o_tlul_a_valid=1 with o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address and o_tlul_a_data unchanged for D+1 cycles, then 0 in the cycle after acceptance. There is exactly one cycle with o_tlul_a_valid=1 and i_tlul_a_ready=1 per transfer. The Access phase lasts 3+D cycles (2+D for a same-cycle response), with correct PRDATA and PSLVERR=0.

checks.title: Orphan responses are discarded
checks.behavior: An i_tlul_d_valid that does not belong to an accepted request has no effect on the APB side.
checks.stimulus: Inject one-cycle i_tlul_d_valid pulses with random i_tlul_d_data, d_opcode, d_error and d_source at these times: while APB is idle (i_apb_psel=0); in a Setup cycle; in A1 while i_tlul_a_ready=0 (before acceptance); in the PREADY cycle and the cycles after a completed response; and during the Access cycle of a local-error transfer. Then run a legal read and a legal write with a prompt device.
checks.expected: An orphan never causes o_apb_pready=1 and never changes o_apb_prdata or o_apb_pslverr. A transfer whose request is accepted after a pre-acceptance orphan completes only after its own response, in the cycle after that response is counted, with that response's data and status. The following legal transfers complete in 3 Access cycles with correct data and PSLVERR=0.

checks.title: Back-to-back transfers with PSEL held high and with idle gaps
checks.behavior: Setup is recognized by levels, so back-to-back transfers are accepted with no idle cycle added. Setup-to-Setup intervals are at their minimum.
checks.stimulus: For every ordered pair of transfer kinds {legal write, legal read, illegal-strobe write, misaligned access}, and each device mode {prompt (a_ready in A1, d_valid in A2), same-cycle response (a_ready and d_valid in A1), prompt with d_error=1}: drive the second Setup in the cycle right after the first transfer's PREADY cycle, keeping i_apb_psel=1 and changing only i_apb_penable to 0. Repeat with 1 idle cycle and with 3 idle cycles of i_apb_psel=0 between the transfers. Use random address and data.
checks.expected: Every transfer completes in order with the correct PRDATA and PSLVERR, and no TL-UL request is made for the illegal ones. With psel held high, the Setup-to-Setup interval is exactly 4 cycles after a prompt-device transfer (also with d_error), 3 cycles after a same-cycle-response transfer, and 2 cycles after a local error. With k idle cycles the interval is the same value plus k. The second transfer's o_tlul_a_valid rises in the cycle after its Setup.

checks.title: Ignored inputs have no effect
checks.behavior: i_apb_pprot, i_apb_pstrb on reads, i_tlul_d_param, i_tlul_d_size, i_tlul_d_sink and i_tlul_d_user do not affect the DUT's behavior.
checks.stimulus: Run a fixed sequence of legal reads, legal writes, illegal-strobe writes, misaligned accesses and d_error responses, with fixed device timing. Repeat it once for each of the 8 i_apb_pprot values, with random i_apb_pstrb on reads, and with random i_tlul_d_param, i_tlul_d_size, i_tlul_d_sink and i_tlul_d_user on every response.
checks.expected: Every output port has the same value in every cycle across all repetitions: TL-UL requests (opcode, address, data, valid timing) and APB completions (o_apb_pready timing, o_apb_prdata, o_apb_pslverr) are identical.

checks.title: Device that never responds blocks the transfer (no timeout)
checks.behavior: Without a TL-UL response the bridge never completes the APB transfer. Reset recovers it.
checks.stimulus: Run a legal read that the device accepts (i_tlul_a_ready=1 in A1) but never answers, with i_tlul_d_valid=0 for 200 cycles while the requester holds i_apb_psel=1 and i_apb_penable=1. Then assert i_rst_n_core, release it, and run a legal write with a prompt device.
checks.expected: o_apb_pready=0 and o_apb_pslverr=0 for all 200 cycles. o_tlul_a_valid=0 from the cycle after acceptance. No new TL-UL request appears. After reset, the write completes normally in 3 Access cycles.

checks.title: Constrained-random traffic with a scoreboard
checks.behavior: Each APB transfer produces exactly one matching TL-UL request (legal ones) and exactly one APB completion that matches the expected result.
checks.stimulus: At least 5000 random transfers: aligned reads and writes with random address and data, plus about 15% illegal-strobe writes and misaligned accesses. Random i_apb_pprot. Idle gaps of 0 to 5 cycles, with psel held high for 0-cycle gaps. Device: i_tlul_a_ready delay 0..8, d_valid delay 0..6 or same-cycle, random d_error/wrong opcode/wrong source in about 10% of responses, random orphan d_valid pulses while no request is pending. Device responses always use d_source=PARA_SRC_ID except for injected errors.
checks.expected: The scoreboard predicts, for each APB transfer in order: no request for an illegal one, otherwise one request with opcode 3'b000 (write) or 3'b100 (read), address = PADDR and data = PWDATA for writes. It predicts the completion: PSLVERR=1 and PRDATA=0 for local or response errors; PRDATA=d_data for a good read; PRDATA=0 for a good write. Every request and completion matches, with no extra or missing ones. All assertions CHK-001 to CHK-016 pass.

assumptions: The APB Requester follows REF-001 (ASM-001): a cycle with i_apb_psel=1 and i_apb_penable=0 happens only at the start of a transfer, after the previous transfer's PREADY cycle. The checkers therefore treat every such rising edge (with i_rst_n_core=1) as a Setup edge with the APB FSM idle.
o_tlul_a_data is compared with i_apb_pwdata only for writes. Its value on a Get is not checked, because the device does not use it.

A TL-UL response is counted when i_tlul_d_valid=1 and o_tlul_d_ready=1 are sampled at the same rising edge. The device model drives each response for exactly one cycle, since o_tlul_d_ready is constantly 1.

Simulation tests run in the default configuration (PARA_ADDR_W=32, PARA_SRC_W=8, PARA_SRC_ID=0, PARA_A_USER_W=1, PARA_D_SINK_W=1, PARA_D_USER_W=1). Checks are written in terms of the parameter names, so they also apply unchanged to another single configuration such as CFG-NARROW.
Reset release is synchronous to i_clk_core (DEP-002). The environment drives the APB Requester and TL-UL device models to idle while i_rst_n_core=0.
